title: Modi's BRICS Invite to Bangladesh PM Revives Hopes for India's September Cricket Tour
excerpt: Bangladesh's Sports Minister backs 'sporting diplomacy' as the BCCI awaits government clearance for a six-match white-ball series that could also reshape the Afghanistan T20I schedule in Delhi.
body:
• India's Government invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the 18th BRICS Summit in September, fueling optimism that India's postponed white-ball tour of Bangladesh will proceed.
  • Bangladesh Sports Minister Aminul Haque publicly backed "sporting diplomacy," saying both nations are ready to bridge recent tensions through cricket.
  • If the Bangladesh tour goes ahead from September 1 to 13, Afghanistan's T20I series against India in Delhi — tentatively set for September 13, 15, and 17 — may be pushed back.
  • FanCode has secured digital streaming rights for the Afghanistan T20Is, breaking JioStar's usual lock on India home internationals, while television rights remain up for grabs.

A Diplomatic Signal Through Cricket

India's September cricket calendar, already among the most congested windows in recent memory, now hinges on a diplomatic development that has little to do with bat and ball. On Friday, news emerged that the Government of India invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the 18th BRICS Summit, to be held in September. The invitation has injected fresh optimism into what has been a fraught saga — India's repeatedly postponed white-ball tour of Bangladesh.

https://x.com/WIONews/status/2080506741142495732

The Bangladesh Cricket Board had announced in January that it would host India for three ODIs and three T20Is, originally scheduled for August-September 2026. The series was itself a rescheduling — the original tour was planned for 2025 but was shelved after diplomatic tensions between the two countries deepened. Those tensions had peaked when the then Yunus-led government withdrew Bangladesh's participation from the T20 World Cup in India, citing security concerns.

"The current government is giving utmost importance to sports diplomacy. We have already spoken to the Indian Embassy, they have also spoken to us, and they are all waiting for India to come to Bangladesh in September."

— Aminul Haque, Bangladesh's State Minister for Youth and Sports

The Tour That Keeps Getting Postponed

The BCB has put the proposed dates at September 1, 3, and 6 for the three ODIs, followed by T20Is on September 9, 12, and 13. If it happens, it would be the first bilateral T20I series between India and Bangladesh played on Bangladeshi soil — a fact not lost on either board.

But significant hurdles remain. The BCB has yet to release its Expression of Interest documents for media rights, having put the sale process on hold earlier this month despite issuing a tender notification. The BCCI, for its part, has maintained silence, with officials saying the board will be guided entirely by the Government of India's advisory.

Bangladesh's Sports Ministry has tried to build momentum. It formed a committee to investigate the reasons behind the T20 World Cup withdrawal, and another to determine whether skipping the tournament was a diplomatic failure. The BCB has also pledged enhanced security measures for the India series if required, according to Cricbuzz.

The Cascading Effect on Afghanistan's Delhi T20Is

The Bangladesh tour's uncertainty has a direct downstream effect on another historic series. The Afghanistan Cricket Board has confirmed to stakeholders that its three-match T20I series against India is on, tentatively scheduled for September 13, 15, and 17 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.

If the Bangladesh tour materializes and runs until September 13, the Afghanistan dates will likely be pushed back. There is very little room for deferment, however. India's Asian Games campaign begins on September 24, and the West Indies white-ball series at home starts on September 27.

The Afghanistan series comes with its own unusual arrangement. Since Afghanistan cannot host international cricket at home, India will technically play as the away team despite the matches being held in Delhi. For the broadcast, JioStar — India's usual home-series broadcaster — will not hold rights. FanCode has secured digital streaming for all three T20Is, while Zee, Sony Sports, and potentially JioStar are expected to compete for linear television rights.

"Our understanding is that there is some sort of agreement between the ACB and the BCCI for the matches. We will handle the media and marketing rights, while the ACB will handle the match-day logistics and operations," Bhairav Shanth, co-founder of ITW Universe, told Cricbuzz.

India's September Squeeze

The Men in Blue are set to finish their Test series against Sri Lanka on August 27. If the Bangladesh tour happens, India would arrive in Dhaka on August 28 and play six white-ball matches through September 13. The Afghanistan T20Is would follow immediately after, before the squad pivots to the Asian Games on September 24 and then hosts the West Indies starting September 27.

It is a punishing schedule that leaves almost no room for rest or injury recovery. The BCCI is expected to make a final call on the Bangladesh tour after receiving government guidance, with the decision likely shaping the broader September calendar for Indian cricket.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For fans in the Indian diaspora, the developments carry significance beyond scheduling. India-Bangladesh cricket has always been more than sport — it reflects the broader state of relations between the two nations. The BRICS invitation and the Sports Minister's public comments suggest a genuine diplomatic thaw, one that could see Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli play what may be their final bilateral series in Bangladesh as they prepare for the 2027 World Cup.

A formal announcement on the Bangladesh tour is expected once the BCCI receives its government advisory. The Afghanistan series announcement, including final dates and broadcast partners, will follow accordingly.
image_caption: India's tour of Bangladesh remains subject to government clearance as the BCCI awaits a formal advisory. The six-match white-ball series could reshape September's cricket calendar, with Afghanistan's T20I dates in Delhi also at stake.
